name: sanding the steps

attributes.attribute: a Cornish New Year's Day ritual
were paid to put sand on house steps
was meant to bring good luck for the coming year

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sanding the steps was a Cornish custom. On New Year's Day in Cornwall, families paid boys to put sand on the steps of houses and other buildings. They did this in the hope of attracting luck for the coming year. The custom is one of the New Year's door rituals found across Britain. A household crossed its own threshold every day, and sand marked that crossing on the first day of the year. The act also gave small work to the boys who carried the sand. The custom shows how a community joined a New Year's wish to an everyday path. Monaghan records the practice as a Cornish New Year's ritual.
